glosses: Parler à tort et à travers.

examples.text: Oh mais je digresse pas du tout ! Ne croyez pas que je blavouille ! ...

Et je ne dirai mie surtout pas blavouiller
Sur tes doigts ouvrageux de jeune fille ancienne
Où je renais enfant chaque fin de semaine
Dans ton nid à poussière au coin d’Aubervilliers

glosses: ohne Substanz und/oder unnötig lange, gewunden und umständlich, wortreich reden oder monologisieren

examples.text: Unser Bürgermeister hat als guter Politiker, der er ist, auf der Bühne länger gelabert; so fiel die Verspätung des Orchesters nicht auf.
‚Ach, laber nicht!‘ (Entgegnung auf Substanzloses)
‚Laber hier nicht rum!‘

glosses: ungezwungen miteinander reden, sich entspannt unterhalten

examples.text: ‚Laber hier nicht rum!‘
Ich habe zufällig eine alte Freundin beim Einkaufen getroffen und mit ihr dann gleich über eine Stunde gelabert.

glosses: sich ungezwungen unterhalten, ein lockeres Gespräch führen

examples.text: Ich habe noch mit jemandem gequatscht.
Der quatscht nun schon den ganzen Abend.
„Die Alte quatscht sich noch mal tot.“ - „Is ja auch ne Rederei hier!“ - (Tetsche)
„Sie haben mir ins Essen gequatscht!“

glosses: To talk rapidly without making much sense.

examples.text: “There you go blatherin’,” said Brindle, intending a mild rebuke.

It was at the unveiling of Sir John Gray's statue. Edmund Dwyer Gray was speaking, blathering away, and here was this old fellow, crabbed-looking old chap, looking at him from under his bushy eyebrows.
On and on he blathered, taking refuge in the one thing he felt lent him superiority: words.

glosses: To say (something foolish or nonsensical); to say (something) in a foolish or overly verbose way.

examples.text: Then, just before the wedding, the old man feels he’s honor bound to tell his future son-in-law the secret of his past; so the damned idiot blathers the whole story of his killing the man and breaking jail!
[…] the church attitude has never been that a teacher should be allowed to blather anything that comes into his head without any accountability at all.
That is the worst of being in an Irish regiment, nothing can be done widout ever so much blather;
Will you cease your blather of mutiny and treason and courts-martial?
With years of proofreading under my belt, I knew exactly the blather and bluster favoured by professional politicians.

1596, Charles Fitzgeoffrey, Sir Francis Drake His Honorable Lifes Commendation, and His Tragicall Deathes Lamentation, Oxford: Joseph Barnes,
[…] on Vlisses Circe did bestowe
A blather, where the windes imboweld were,

glosses: To speak at length on a trivial subject.

examples.text: She got home and started wittering about some religious cult she’d just heard about.
When people witter on about pollution nowadays, I think of the days when going to school in broad daylight, I couldn't see my feet in the London smog. I had to feel the kerb with my front bike wheel.

glosses: to make sure, inform, or declare.
